test(markup): pin a negated attribute byte for byte against the reference (rich-color-9ga)

The SGR 22 the ticket measured was already gone: a5ef4b92 (#117) made
Style.toSgrCodes write only the attributes that are on. Nothing pinned it.
negated-attribute puts [bold red]a[not bold]b[/not bold]c[/] in the

every existing case reproduced unchanged. Mutating toSgrCodes to emit 22
for a false attribute turns it red.

The ticket's own [red]..[not bold] shape cannot go in yet: the encoder

feat(host): App, the runtime that takes the terminal and hands it back on every exit (rich-runtime-fna.3) (#198)

* feat(host): App, the runtime that takes the terminal and hands it back on every exit (rich-runtime-fna.3)

App paints one renderable per frame on an alternate or inline surface,
repaints on refresh() and resize, suspends through the host, and undoes the
alternate screen, hidden cursor and raw mode on stop, a throwing frame, and
every way the program can end under it.

TerminalHost gains onExit and suspend. The node host hears exit, SIGINT,
SIGTERM, SIGHUP and uncaughtExceptionMonitor, keeps each ending's default
outcome, and suspends by SIGTSTP with a timer holding the loop until SIGCONT.

installTraceback now throws unhandled rejections into the uncaught channel,
so node's monitor phase restores the terminal before every report prints.

rich-explore runs on App, with Ctrl+Z to suspend.

* fix(host): suspend stops the job, signals coexist with signal-exit, a program's end leaves run unsettled (rich-runtime-fna.3)

From the /code-review high pass on PR #198:

- NodeTerminalHost.suspend sends SIGTSTP to the process group, as the
  terminal sends Ctrl+Z, so a launcher (npm run, sh -c) stops with the
  program and the shell takes the terminal. A signal to one's own group is
  delivered inside kill, so suspend resolves when the call returns: no
  SIGCONT wait and no keep-alive timer, and a discarded SIGTSTP (no job
  control) no longer strands the app suspended.
- onExit's signal listeners are prepended, so a listener keeping the same
  raise-only-when-alone rule (signal-exit) finds itself alone and raises
  the signal instead of both standing down.
- When the program ends under the app, run() does not settle, so no code
  after it runs inside a crash's report and exit.
- An inline frame that blanks rows below it rewinds to its own height.
- installTraceback raises an unhandled rejection after its other listeners
  have heard it.
- rich-explore ends the app with a reducer's error again.

* docs(host): an inline app starts on the cursor's line, not below it (rich-runtime-fna.3)
